title: Exception Handling
description: Catching failures, throwing your own, and custom exceptions.

questions.explanation: Index 5 doesn't exist → exception → the catch runs instead of crashing.

questions.prompt: What's wrong with this catch order?
options: Exception catches everything first — the second catch is unreachable
questions.explanation: Specific catches must come before general ones, or the general one swallows everything.

questions.prompt: Order what happens when an exception is thrown in a try block.
lines: Rest of the try block is skipped
questions.explanation: Thrown → try abandoned → catch handles → finally cleans up.

questions.prompt: To raise an exception yourself, use ___.
questions.explanation: throw = raise one now. throws = declare one might escape.

questions.prompt: Match each keyword to its job.
Which JavaScript is the same idea?
questions.explanation: Both try something risky, both land in catch with a friendly message.

questions.prompt: What does this print, in order?
questions.explanation: A prints, the throw skips to catch (B), and finally (C) always runs.

options: IOException is checked — must be caught or declared with throws
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions are the compiler's rule: catch it or declare it.

questions.prompt: A custom checked exception is made by ___ the Exception class.
questions.explanation: extends Exception = checked. extends RuntimeException = unchecked.

questions.prompt: Which Java matches this custom exception?
questions.explanation: Both extend the exception base and pass the message up with super.
